Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an internal green light to run a production-like POC for our recommendation engine starting the week of 2025-02-10. Before we lock dates with our engineering team, procurement needs a clear picture of the capacity you can provision and whether Redwood can put a provisional hold on nodes while we finalize terms.

High-level ask:
- Target start: 2025-02-10
- Expected steady-state: ~120 A100-equivalent GPU slots for the 6-week POC
- Burst requirement: additional ~40 slots during peak evaluation days

Attached is a quick demand outline (demand_outline_Q1.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can posture a soft hold or reserved window for the SequoiaAI POC, and what the risk profile is if we need to move the start by +/- 2 weeks?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants a short note by Friday.

Thanks,

Quick asks for the ops check:
- Can we guarantee 120 A100-equivalent slots in us-west-2 for a 6-week POC starting 2025-02-10? If not guaranteed, what split of guaranteed / burst can we offer?

On Wed, Jan 22, 2025 at 9:12 AM Marcus DuBois <marcus.d@sequoiaai.com> wrote:
> Hi Rishi —
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

Rishi — thanks for the tag. Initial ops read below after a quick inventory sweep (see attached capacity_snapshot_Q1.csv). Short summary:

- Us-west-2 current free headroom: ~95 A100-equivalent slots today (fleet-wide across dedicated and standby pools).
- We can commit a hard reservation of ~80 slots for the POC start date with standard reserved capacity contract (30-day notice + billing commit).
- For the remaining ~40 slots to reach the requested 120, we can offer burst/beta capacity sourced from transient nodes; that would be best-effort and exposed to preemption during infra rebalancing or higher-priority commits.
- Soft hold option: we can earmark an additional 30 slots (no billing commitment) for up to 21 days. Earmark does not prevent the scheduler from reassigning if utilization forces it, but we will prioritize SequoiaAI over new uncommitted orders.

Risks & mitigations:
- If they shift +-2 weeks, guaranteed 80 still holds. For the additional 40-40 (burst + earmark), availability is a function of incoming renewals and market demand; propose a canary of a 2-week early start for validation.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm whether SequoiaAI can accept 80 guaranteed + 40 burst + 30 earmark (i.e., 80/40/30).
2) If they want more guarantee, we need a committed reserved pool (contract change) — ops will need a signed order by 2025-01-31 to guarantee 120.

Attaching capacity_snapshot_Q1.csv with the node inventory breakout.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Rishi / team —

Thanks Laura — adding a quick deployment note from SE/solutions:
- For the POC performance profile Marcus shared, they should plan to use our deduped KV cache and batch size 64 / seq-len 2048 to reduce per-token footprint. That will materially lower the A100-equivalent count during steady-state (we should model both conservative and optimized cases).
- Sizing suggestion: run a short load dress rehearsal 7 days prior to start to validate burst behavior. If rehearsal hits >80% of requested peak, ops will trigger pre-allocations.

Operational asks for procurement/legal:
- If they accept the 80-guaranteed + 40-burst + 30-earmark split, we can lay out a mutual action plan (MAP) with checkpoints: SOW sign by 2025-01-31, load dress rehearsal week of 2025-02-03, POC start 2025-02-10.

I'll draft a brief MAP and attach to the SOW.

—Monica
